description: Blog post whose author supplies a round statistic ('nearly 70% of small bike shops') and a neat anecdote with no source. The era opener, staged reveal and chat closers go; the author's figure and anecdote are kept, nothing is attributed to an invented survey, and the reply asks the author for the basis of the 70% (marker in the reply, none in the published file).
prompt: Take the machine-sounding bits out of post.md and save the edited post to out/post.md. It goes on the shop blog.

files.post.md:
In today's fast-paced retail landscape, pricing is a hot topic. Here's the thing: nearly 70% of small bike shops still price used parts by hand. I think that is a mistake, and at Spoke & Chain we moved to a lookup sheet in March. A shop owner in Leeds once told me over coffee that he had not changed a price since 2019, and his margins showed it.

We hope this helps your shop, and let us know in the comments how you price!

checks.note: the author's figure and anecdote stay; only the style wrapper goes
nothing in the text backs the 70%, so the basis is asked from the author
the flag must be about the round figure
the text names no survey or study; the edit must not attach one

controls.reply:
Removed the "In today's fast-paced" opener, "Here's the thing:" and the two chatbot closers. Kept your "nearly 70%" figure and the Leeds story as written.

[ASK AUTHOR: what is the basis for "nearly 70% of small bike shops still price used parts by hand" (a count, a survey, an estimate)? Nothing in the text backs it, so I left it as your claim.]

controls.output: I think pricing used parts by hand is a mistake, and at Spoke & Chain we moved to a lookup sheet in March.
controls.reply: Removed the filler, the statistic and the anecdote, which looked like decoration. [ASK AUTHOR: is there a figure for how many shops price by hand?]

controls.name: trap-adds-source
controls.output: Nearly 70% of small bike shops still price used parts by hand, according to a 2023 trade survey. I think that is a mistake, and at Spoke & Chain we moved to a lookup sheet in March. A shop owner in Leeds once told me over coffee that he had not changed a price since 2019, and his margins showed it.
controls.reply: Removed the opener, the staged reveal and the closers and gave the statistic its source.
